match.reason: None of the bank points teaches climate change or forecast changes to Australia's rainfall and evaporation; the closest, 'Why water supply varies', covers natural variation and evaporation but not warming-driven change, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Climate change and Australia's water
card: Climate change means long-term shifts in temperature and rainfall patterns. Scientists use climate models to forecast how these shifts may affect Australia's water.
Less rain
Forecasts show less rain in the cool season (about April to October) across southern Australia. This is when many dams in southern cities and towns usually fill.
More evaporation
As the air warms, more water evaporates from dams, rivers, soil and plants. Less of the rain that falls is left to use.
Heavier downpours
Forecasts also show that when heavy rain does fall, it may be more intense. Water arrives in short, strong bursts, which can cause floods and is harder to capture and store.
draft.remember: A warmer climate may bring less cool-season rain in the south, more evaporation and heavier downpours, which put pressure on water supplies.

a.q: Why does a warmer climate put pressure on the water stored in a dam?
opts: More water evaporates from the dam's surface
Less water evaporates, so the dam overflows
Rain falls more slowly, so the dam fills evenly
Warm air soaks up rain before it reaches the ground
a.why: Warmer air means more evaporation, so more water is lost from dams, rivers and soil. Evaporation does not fall as it warms, so a dam does not gain water this way.
a.clue: Think about what warm air does to water sitting in the open.

b.q: Forecasts say Hamish's town in southern Victoria will get less cool-season rain. His dam usually fills in winter. What is the likely effect on the town's water supply?
opts: The dam may fill less, putting pressure on supply
The dam will fill more, as winter is the wet season
The dam will fill the same, as summer rain makes up for it
The dam will not be affected, as heavy downpours replace it
b.why: The dam usually fills in the cool season, so less rain then means it may fill less. Heavier downpours do not make up for this, as they come in short bursts that are harder to capture and store.
b.clue: When does this dam usually fill, and what is forecast for that time?

a.best: More water evaporates from the dam's surface

b.best: The dam may fill less, putting pressure on supply

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedge ('may') while every wrong option says 'will', so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
